gaps.fact: Over 90 per cent of Alsace wine is made from white grapes: no chapter, article or question gives the share.
Goldert, one of the Court's four example Grands Crus, is named nowhere in the Codex; Schlossberg, Brand and Hengst are taught and asked.

Domaine Weinbach, Marcel Deiss, Hugel et Fils, Pierre Sparr and Zind-Humbrecht are in the article and asked in no question of either bank; only Trimbach is asked, through its Rosacker and Geisberg and Osterberg sites.

Baeckeoffe, Flammkuchen and smoky cured meats as partners: Baeckeoffe is only a wrong option in i-t5ub4hmj, which asks the dish and not the wine, and no stem pairs an Alsace wine with tarte flambée, Baeckeoffe, bacon or sausage.

Crémant d'Alsace as an alternative, cost effective source of traditional method sparkling wine: the Codex gives its grapes, its ageing and its rank as the second largest French sparkling appellation, but never the value case a sommelier makes for it.

courtUpdates.printed: *The fifth is now Pinot Noir as of the 2022 vintage.; Exceptions to the Alsace Grand Cru AOP grape variety rule: One of the Grand Crus uses Sylvaner, two of them allow blending, two allow red wine.
courtUpdates.now: A third Grand Cru, Vorbourg at Rouffach, was opened to Pinot Noir in 2024, beside Hengst and Kirchberg de Barr (2022 vintage), so three Grands Crus now allow red wine. The Codex carries it in the Village chapter (fact 1), the Village stem c-se3gyec3, the article's law and grapes and its exceptions card.
courtUpdates.source: INAO, cahier des charges Alsace Grand Cru as amended in 2024 (the article's own source list; no search spent on it).

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 58 (Alsace), Village 19 (Alsace), 77 in all. Beyond the map, Producers & Icons asks two Trimbach sites, Food & Pairing pairs off-dry Riesling or Gewurztraminer with Southeast Asian food, and Geography & Maps and Germany set Alsace against Baden across the Rhine. Both columns are well served: the departments, the rain shadow, the soil mosaic, every grape the Court names, the Grand Cru count and every exception, the flûte, Edelzwicker and Gentil, Vendange Tardive and Sélection de Grains Nobles with their must weights; the thin cells are Goldert, the producer roll beyond Trimbach, the Court's three dishes and the value of Crémant. No factual error found: AOC 1962, Schlossberg 1975, Crémant 1976, the late harvest law of 1984, Kaefferkopf 2007, fifty three appellations in 2011, Tokay Pinot Gris retired with the 2007 vintage, the must weights (235 and 257, 276 and 306 grams a litre), nine months on the lees and twelve from tirage for Crémant, and the sweetness indication from the 2021 vintage all hold. One reading to carry: the Court says a varietal label means 100 per cent of the grape, and the article adds that Pinot Blanc may legally include Auxerrois; both stand. One search spent, on an Alsace Premier Cru tier: no approval was found, so the tier remains a proposal, as the article says; Vorbourg is taken from the article's dated source.
